clue.text: Bag ferret beside bay maybe

parts.note: a hob is a male ferret
by means next to, beside
a bay is a reddish-brown horse, so an example of a horse

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs a ferret into a sack next to a bay horse, or by the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bag' as in 'not my bag': one's pet interest. A hob is the male ferret.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone's bag is their favourite pursuit or pet subject, which is what a hobbyhorse is.

clue.text: Henry likes tanks going round in European capital

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the word in
tanks as a verb means collapses or fails, so the letters of likes are broken up

explanation.surface: A man called Henry enjoys watching tanks circling inside a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tanks' looks like military vehicles but is a verb, to collapse; the jumble ELSKI then goes round 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland, a European country.

clue.text: Get free headgear in English Home Counties

indicators.note: the headgear sits in the English and Home Counties letters

parts.note: the Home Counties around London are in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
a cap is a piece of headgear

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a free hat somewhere in the English Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in England's South East, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to get free of captivity is to break out or flee.

clue.text: Went by horse and by boat, as stated

indicators.note: stated means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: went by boat, pulling oars, is rowed

explanation.surface: A traveller describes a journey made partly on horseback and partly by water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' serves both halves: went by horse, and went by boat (rowed), which is said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of ride: someone who went on horseback travelled in the saddle.

clue.text: Struggle to control side that's chuffed

indicators.note: to control is to hold, so the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: to strain is to struggle
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A team struggles to keep a side in check and is pleased with itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chuffed' looks like British slang for pleased, but here it means puffing like a locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: a locomotive powered by steam makes a chuffing noise as it puffs along.

clue.text: Taxi left people over for gondola

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A taxi dropped people off who had come for a ride in a Venetian gondola.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns RACE into ECAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging gondolas are the passenger cabins on an aerial ropeway up a mountain.

clue.text: Afghan sometimes reserves old vehicle

indicators.note: reserves means keeps back inside, so the letters are held within the two words

explanation.surface: An Afghan hound occasionally keeps a vintage car for itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a two-wheeled horse-drawn cab of Victorian times, now historic.

clue.text: First person in Paris meets Rolling Stone and gushes

parts.note: je is French for I, the first person singular

indicators.note: rolling over means turned round, so the abbreviation reads backwards

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A Frenchman meets one of the Rolling Stones and is effusive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stone' looks like the band; 'Rolling' reverses ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: streams of water spurting out are spurts or spouts.

clue.text: Drive off in Open but go too far

indicators.note: one word placed in the other

parts.note: overt means open, unconcealed
to shoo is to drive away

explanation.surface: A golfer drives off at the Open championship but hits the ball too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive off' and 'Open' suggest golf, but they mean shoo away and overt.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to pass beyond a target or limit, as a runway landing might.

clue.text: Fast car avoids Shell

indicators.note: avoids means keeps clear of, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: a carapace is the hard shell of a crab or tortoise

explanation.surface: A speedy car steers clear of a Shell petrol station.
explanation.walkthrough: Shell looks like the oil company; it is CARAPACE, and the car is taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: done at speed, quickly.

clue.text: Book American food and cost of travel

parts.note: US stands for American, of the United States
fare is food

explanation.surface: Someone reserves American food and pays for the journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The ticket price for a ride on a public road vehicle is what one pays to travel.

clue.text: In his element, old sailor recalled lots of maps

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole is read backwards
the sailor is in his element

parts.note: a sailor's natural element is the sea
an old salt is a veteran sailor

explanation.surface: A veteran seaman, happy at sea, remembers all the charts he used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns SE(SALT)A round.
explanation.definitionFit: Books of maps, in the plural, collect many charts together.

clue.text: Layer, say, reflected old enclosure

parts.note: a hen is a layer of eggs

indicators.note: reflected as in a mirror, so the letters are turned round

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A layer of rock is reflected upon in an ancient walled site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' means one that lays: a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a prehistoric circular earthwork such as Stonehenge.

clue.text: Calcium current in graves? Lots of those here

parts.note: Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium

indicators.note: the current goes in the graves

parts.note: tombs are graves
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: Calcium and current flowing among graves: a strange chemistry scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'those' refers back to 'graves': underground burial galleries hold many.
explanation.definitionFit: Underground burial galleries, as in Rome, contain great numbers of tombs.

clue.text: Make clear fancy articles to engage youths on vacation

indicators.note: to engage is to take on, so the jumbled letters hold the other pair
fancy means elaborate or imaginative, so the letters are rearranged
vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters of the word stay

explanation.surface: Elaborate pieces of writing are needed to employ young people during their holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' means emptied of the middle letters; 'fancy' gives CRTALISE, which engages the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make definite and clear-cut, as when ideas harden into form.

clue.text: What Bo-Peep didn't do? Record her day in Slough

indicators.note: the record, her and day go in the slough

parts.note: to slough a skin is to shed it
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme puzzle: a record of her day in the Berkshire town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Bo-Peep lost her sheep, so she failed to guard them. Slough is a town near London; here it means to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: Bo-Peep lost her sheep, so she failed to herd and guard her flock.

clue.text: Romeo has trouble with a Yankee bearing 17 perhaps

parts.note: R is Romeo in the radio alphabet
to ail is to trouble
Y is Yankee in the radio alphabet
carriage is bearing, deportment

explanation.surface: Romeo struggles with an American's demeanour.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is WAGON-LIT, a sleeping car on a train, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sleeping car is one kind of passenger vehicle on a train.

clue.text: Sleeper with new books acquired earlier

indicators.note: acquired means took in, so the first letters take the other word inside

parts.note: lit is short for literature, books
ago means earlier, in the past

explanation.surface: Someone sleeping with new books bought a while ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeper' looks like a person, but it is a sleeping car on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A continental railway sleeping car; a sleeper is a train with berths.

clue.text: Amateur artist rebuked about northern web designer, say

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word goes round the letter

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to rebuke

explanation.surface: An amateur artist is scolded for a northern website design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'web designer' sounds like a computer job; it is a spider. CHID is archaic for chided.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a spider spins webs and is one of the eight-legged invertebrates.

clue.text: Brief answer to clue 'Cracking nuts'

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: an en, also called a nut, is a printer's space, so nuts gives two of them
in crosswords an answer entered in the grid is called a light

explanation.surface: Someone asks for the short answer to a crossword clue about cracking nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' is a verb, to inform. LIGHT cracks EN EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to inform someone, giving them the facts they need.

clue.text: State capital's landau in need of repair

indicators.note: something in need of repair is broken, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A city's horse-drawn carriage is falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Luanda is the capital city of Angola, a state in south-west Africa.

clue.text: Train, or part of one

definitions.meaning: to train is to tutor or instruct
a railway carriage is part of a train

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to tutor someone, and a carriage forming part of a train.

clue.text: Keen to defend old president's goodness

indicators.note: to defend is to protect by surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry
Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: Someone eager to defend a former president's good character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager, but it is the verb to wail.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclamation: both express surprise, like 'my word' or 'gosh'.

clue.text: When out of cash girl left station

indicators.note: out of means removed from, so these letters leave the word

parts.note: as means when
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: When she ran out of money, a girl left the railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' looks like a railway one; it is a television station.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a television or radio broadcaster's band, a broadcasting station.

clue.text: Tom, say, boxes right lug

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the letter is put in a box of other letters

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, an example

explanation.surface: A tom cat boxes a right ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lug' looks like an ear and 'boxes' like punching; lug is to haul.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to haul or carry something heavy and awkward.

clue.text: Strike stops the queen getting to that place

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so the strike goes into the gap

parts.note: to hit is to strike
R is regina, queen

explanation.surface: A strike halts the queen on her way to a destination.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic adverb of direction: to or towards a place named.

clue.text: Start to take blame for ambush?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: Is beginning to accept blame a kind of ambush?
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a snare or ambush is a device for catching someone unawares.

clue.text: Supporters-in-arms notice Republican units gathering

indicators.note: gathering means gathering in, so the outer letters take the notice inside

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a unit, so units are two of them
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Comrades-in-arms spot Republican units massing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters-in-arms' plays on 'brothers-in-arms': the bones that support the forearm.
explanation.definitionFit: The forearm bones, each called a radius, support the arms.

clue.text: When to throw parties with this setter?

definitions.text: When to throw parties with this setter?

indicators.note: to throw is to scramble or fling about, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The setter asks when the best moment is to host parties with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure hours outside work are the natural moments for hosting celebrations.
